findings.reason: as written a worker can deliver the registry node as code-plus-tests alone, leaving the on-disk artifacts on the pre-alias digest while the pin rows copy it, so the plan must name the artifact re-authoring in the registry node's scope (the drive-map node names its own re-authoring at plan.html:490-491, this node does not).
findings.text: the registry node "writes only the producer module, the shared digest function in artifact_geometry.py and their tests", but the plan states recording the per-phase representation aliases "moves the registry digest" (plan.html:415) and that the selection node's JT-60SA pin rows are "copied from the two artifacts as they stand once that registry node has landed" (plan.html:480-482); the landed producer bakes the registry digest into each artifact (imas_ambix/gs/description_artifact.py:364,375 author_jt60sa_machine_artifacts), so completing the registry changes every artifact's embedded digest and the artifacts must be re-authored at that node or the copied pin rows freeze a stale digest and the stamp fails — yet no node is assigned to re-run the producer

response_events.reason: Plan v401 (commit after 4e9fa13f): no artifact is stored between nodes; author_jt60sa_machine_artifacts authors both on demand, so the selection node authors them at its own base (carrying the drive-map and registry changes) and copies its pins from those, and one of its tests re-authors both and asserts each matches its pinned row.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the registry node's declared scope omits the artifact re-authoring that its own digest change forces, while the selection node's pin copy at plan.html:480-482 depends on the artifacts having been re-authored.
